title: Tax on shares and equity mutual funds — capital gains (FY 2026-27)
publisher: Summarised from Income Tax Department rules and Budget 2026-27 coverage
text: When you sell listed shares or equity mutual funds at a profit, the gain is taxed separately from your salary. If you held them for 12 months or less it is a short-term gain taxed at a flat 20%. If you held them for more than 12 months it is a long-term gain: the first ₹1.25 lakh of long-term gains in a financial year is exempt and the rest is taxed at a flat 12.5%. Budget 2026-27 left these rates unchanged. These special rates apply on top of your normal slab tax, and the Section 87A rebate that makes tax zero up to ₹12 lakh does not cancel tax on these gains. Losses can be set off against gains (short-term losses against both kinds, long-term losses only against long-term gains) and carried forward for eight years if you file your return on time. The Income-tax Act, 2025, effective 1 April 2026, renumbers the sections (111A, 112, 112A), so ITR forms may cite new section numbers. Dividends are taxed at your slab rate. This is an educational summary — check the rules for debt funds, gold and property, which differ.
summary_hinglish: Shares/equity mutual fund ka munafa 12 mahine se kam rakhne par 20% short-term tax lagta hai, 12 mahine se zyada par ₹1.25 lakh tak chhoot aur uske upar 12.5% long-term tax.
